_doc: Graveyards and the trade in death (world/graveBook.js, world/graveArt.js, world/townPlanner.js, world/innerMap/graves.js, systems/graveyards.js, ui/innerMapGraves.js, ui/actionMenu/graveyards.js). Every town keeps a burial ground on settlement.graveyard: its churchyard (planned beside the church or temple, or on the edge of a village) with yard[type] = [width, depth] tiles (the planner shrinks it to fit): an iron railing along its street front with a gate in the middle, plots two tiles wide (the marker at the head, the mound beside it) in pairs of rows with a walk between. A grave is one townsperson who died (systems/townsfolk.js), with their name, dates, cause and a marker for their station. Graves are leased for a term; when one runs out and no kin renews it, the plot is cleared and the bones go to the charnel house. The player can consecrate a building lot of theirs as a burial ground and lease its plots to the town's families.
_classes: A dead townsperson's station, from their role (or retired trade): it decides the marker, the coffin, the lease the family wants and the goods buried with them.
_terms: Grave leases: years (null = in perpetuity) and the price as a multiple of a ten-year lease. A family that can't pay its usual term takes the next shorter.
_pricing: A ten-year plot costs plotBase[type] x scarcity, scarcity = (targetYears / years of room)^elasticity clamped to [min, max], years of room = free plots in town (the churchyard's and every private ground's) / the town's deaths a year. The parish charges parishMult of that; a private ground charges its owner's policy (cheap/fair/dear).
_markers: What a grave is marked with, and how it ages. inputs: what raising it takes from the town's market stock (a cross from wood, a headstone from stone). Wooden markers rot to a bare mound after rotYears, then to nothing (unmarked) after goneYears; stone weathers to headstone_old after oldYears and headstone_broken after brokenYears. tiles: its footprint [w, h] on the map (an art manifest overrides it).
_art: The painted sprites: artDir/<id>.png, 128 px a tile, each fitted to its tiles box and stood on its bottom, centred (scripts/make_graves.py). build:data merges artDir/manifest.json in as `art` ({ id: { w, h, tilesW, tilesH } }); a marker with no art yet is drawn as the old dug-grave mound until it lands. A grave dug in the last freshYears shows its mound beside the marker.
_coffins: A coffin takes `planks` planks a size from the town's stock (the coffin-maker's timber); none to be had, the dead go in a shroud.
_seed: A town's churchyard is not new when the player first sees it: seedFill of its plots hold the dead of the years before (seedRecent of them recent, on leases still running; the rest old graves held in perpetuity).
_town: When the churchyard is full, the sexton clears the graves whose leases have run out (the bones to the charnel house). Still full for newGroundAfterYears, and its purse holds twice newGroundCost[type], the town opens a new ground beside the old (newGroundShare more plots). With nowhere to lie, the dead go in the common pit.
_consecrate: Consecrating a lot of yours as a burial ground: a fee to the town's temple (into the town's purse), refused where your standing in the realm is below minStanding. Its plots are laid in rows within the lot.
_leasing: Your ground's leases: each lapse is renewed by kin still in town at the class's renew chance (if the purse can pay); unrenewed, it lies lapsed until cleared. A sexton you hire clears one for sextonFee[type] (to the town's purse); or dig it up yourself on the town map.
_bones: Bones: one set from every grave cleared. The charnel house of any town takes them for nothing (piety); a city's or capital's bone-grinder buys them (boneBase x glut, paid from the town's purse; the glut eases glutDecay a day). The charnel sells its own to you at charnelPrice.
_mill: A bone mill of your own, built on a lot of yours: cost gold (the builders' wages, into the town's purse) and inputs (bought from the town's market stock at its price), standing after days. It grinds grindPerDay sets of bones a day into mealPerBone bone meal each.
_meal: Bone meal sells to the town's farmers (mealBase x farmFactor[type] x glut, from the purse). Every unit spread on their fields raises the town's soil by soilPerUnit (to the harvest's soil max): next harvest's yields follow the soil.
_ossuary: An ossuary shrine on a lot of yours: cost gold and stone, and foundBones sets of bones to found it (more may be laid in after). The town's people come to pray for their dead: perVisit[type] each, visitors a day = min(maxVisitors[type], bones / bonesPerVisitor), paid from the town's purse.
_gravedigger: The sexton's work, a day labour: each burial and each clearing in town leaves a grave to dig; you dig up to maxPerDay of them for payPerGrave[type] each from the town's purse, at an energy cost. The town's own sexton digs sextonPerDay a day when you don't.
_kin: Your own dead (children, a spouse, the heads of your House before you): laid to rest in a ground of yours (no lease: they lie in perpetuity) or the parish churchyard at its fee; a coffin and marker of your choice bought from the town's stock at its price. kinMarkers: what you may raise over them.
_robbery: Robbing a grave (taking its goods, or digging it up without the right): a theft (systems/containers.js stealOdds and stealGoods: the odds by witnesses, guards, the hour and the worth; the fine, the record and the cells), with `reputation` standing lost on top if caught; what you take is hot. Digging up a lapsed grave on your own ground is no crime.
_goods: The goods of death, registered into the player's goods table: bones and bone meal trade only through the charnel house, the bone-grinder, your mill and the farmers (noMarket); grave goods (trinkets buried with the dead) sell anywhere.

BONES.name: Bones
BONES.description: A set of bones from a cleared grave. The charnel house keeps them; a bone-grinder buys them; a bone mill grinds them to meal.

BONE_MEAL.name: Bone Meal
BONE_MEAL.description: Bones ground fine: a fertiliser the farmers spread on tired fields.

GRAVE_GOODS.name: Grave Goods
GRAVE_GOODS.description: Rings, buckles and keepsakes buried with the dead.

respects: You stand a while by the grave of {name}.
You bow your head over {name}'s grave.
You say a word for {name}, {years} in the ground.
text.unmarked: An old grave, its marker long gone. No one living knows who lies here.
